questions.q: What is the AWS root user, and how should it be used according to this lesson?
options: The all-powerful identity created with every account, tied to the sign-up email — locked away behind MFA and reserved for setup/closure, not everyday work
A generic shared login every employee should use daily
An identity that only has read-only permissions
A temporary identity that expires 24 hours after account creation
questions.explain: AWS's own guidance is to secure the root user with MFA and avoid using it for day-to-day work — use IAM users or roles instead.

questions.q: Why do real organizations typically end up with multiple AWS accounts instead of just one?
options: Separate accounts give a hard security and billing boundary — a mistake or breach in one account can't reach resources in a different account
AWS technically limits every account to five total resources
Multiple accounts are required to unlock access to the console
It's purely a historical convention with no actual security benefit
questions.explain: Splitting environments or teams into separate accounts creates a real isolation boundary, not just a logical one within shared IAM.

questions.q: What does AWS Organizations let you do?
options: Group multiple AWS accounts under one management account, arrange them into Organizational Units, and apply policy in bulk
Merge multiple AWS accounts into a single account automatically
Replace the need for IAM entirely within every member account
Grant every member account unlimited free usage
questions.explain: Organizations is specifically for managing many accounts as a group — consolidated billing, OUs, and SCPs — not merging them.

questions.q: What does a Service Control Policy (SCP) do?
options: Sets the maximum permissions any identity in an account or OU can ever have, regardless of what that account's own IAM policies allow
Grants every IAM user in the account administrator access automatically
Controls only which Region an account's root user can log in from
Determines the visual theme of the AWS Management Console for that account
questions.explain: An SCP is a guardrail ceiling — it can only restrict, never grant, permissions beyond what IAM policies inside the account allow.

questions.q: What does consolidated billing, part of AWS Organizations, provide?
options: One invoice across every member account, with volume discounts calculated across the Organization's combined usage
A separate invoice per IAM user within each account
Free usage for every account in the Organization
Automatic conversion of Reserved Instances into Spot Instances
questions.explain: Consolidated billing combines invoicing and volume pricing across every account under the Organization's management account.
